messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: GPU pool saturation detected for eu-west-1-hosted (severity: high). autoscaler hitting configured max. queue size growing. paging ryan_oncall :rotating_light:
ryan_oncall: on it. seeing sustained queue growth on model-pool-2, avg queue length ~420 requests, 95th latency token gen spiking. starting checklist.
maria_prodeng: is this correlated with the config push from last night? I saw a batch config change in the deploy logs.
alex_mlinfra: yep, last deploy adjusted continuous batching params and prefix cache policy (change set id cs-2026-03-12-09). I pulled the diff: max_wait_ms lowered from 40->10 and prefix_cache_ttl reduced 600s->60s.
jitendra_runtime: that explains why prefix cache hit-rate dropped. With smaller TTL and lower batching window, we get more small batches and cache churn -> lower throughput -> more GPU tasks queued.
ryan_oncall: good catch. immediate mitigation options?
samir_ops: we can bump pool capacity manually, but autoscaler is maxed at 12 gpus. we have spare nodes in the region but not allocated. we can request a hot-add up to +4 if approved (takes ~4-6m).
ryan_oncall: do it. @samir_ops request hot add now. also set traffic fallback to cpu-optimized smaller model for non-prem customers to reduce pressure.
samir_ops: submitted hot add request: request-id rq-8421. provisioning started.
emily_csm: heads-up: two customers (acme-analytics, greenfin) are creating support tickets about 5xx/latency. I pinged them saying we're investigating.
alex_mlinfra: I'm running a quick canary rollback of the batch config to previous values in a single pool to validate. command:
```
redwoodctl config apply --pool model-pool-2 --file batch-config-prev.yaml --dry-run=false
```
ryan_oncall: nice. monitor traffic to canary and queue behavior.
jitendra_runtime: observed prefix cache miss rate jump from 8%->46% across pools after the change. KV cache eviction also increased. if cache TTL is 60s, churn is huge for steady traffic patterns. revert TTL and max_wait_ms and we should see hit-rate recover.
alex_mlinfra: canary applied to model-pool-2-a. immediate metrics: queue length down from 420->190, request latency improving, throughput up ~28%.
ryan_oncall: good. proceed with staged rollback to all pools. staged batch: model-pool-2-b then c. do not change autoscaler config yet.
samir_ops: hot-add complete. +3 gpus added to pool (now max desired temporarily 15). takes some load off.
emily_csm: customers reporting partial recovery. sending status update: "We're mitigating, expected recovery in next 15-30m".
ryan_oncall: path forward: 1) roll back batching/prefix-cache config to the previous working values (done staged), 2) clear prefix cache on nodes to remove churn artifacts, 3) monitor for 30m, 4) if stable, scale down extra GPUs and reopen autoscaler to normal.
jitendra_runtime: command to clear cache (run one-per-node):
```
redwoodctl exec --pool model-pool-2 --cmd "rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/prefix_cache/* && systemctl restart redwood-runtime"
```
alex_mlinfra: running cache flush on pool-2-a,b,c in parallel. will post logs.
ryan_oncall: also enable temporary request-level rate cap for non-enterprise routes at 1rps per token to throttle noisy traffic while we stabilize. dev-deploy-bot, can you flip the feature-flag?
dev-deploy-bot: feature-flag toggled: routing.rate_limit.non_enterprise = 1rps (applied to eu-west-1).
samir_ops: after rollback and cache flush, queue length trending down to ~30-60. autoscaler now healthy and accepting scale-down.
emily_csm: acme-analytics confirmed decreased errors, logs show 503->200 transition. greenfin still seeing some retries but improved.
ryan_oncall: putting an incident note: root cause suspected regression in continuous batching params + TTL change causing prefix cache miss storm leading to reduced throughput and queue accumulation, compounded by autoscaler hit limit.
maria_prodeng: create follow-up: revert PR, add test coverage for prefix_cache_ttl sensitivity, add a perf guard for batch params that triggers rollback if QPS/latenct degrades >15% in 5m.
jitendra_runtime: will add an automated smoke eval that runs after config deploys measuring cache hit-rate and token throughput.
alex_mlinfra: will file a config-rollout rule: any change to continuous batching must run on a canary pool for 20m with threshold checks.
ryan_oncall: handoff: I'm going offline in 25m. @maria_prodeng will be acting incident lead for next shift. leave runbook and current checkpoints.
maria_prodeng: acknowledged. current state: all pools rolled back, prefix caches flushed, hot-add GPUs will be drained after 30m if stable. affected customers notified. ops follow-up: finalize autoscaler upper-limit changes?
samir_ops: propose increasing autoscaler soft limit +2 for peak windows and add a scaling buffer policy. will open change request CR-4769.
emily_csm: drafting customer postmortem note for impacted customers with ETA for RCA.
ryan_oncall: closing loop: please capture timeline and metrics. I'll attach graphs of queue length, cache hit-rate, and autoscaler events to the ticket. if anything regresses ping oncall.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: incident-1802123456 created, severity: high, status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem assignee: maria_prodeng.
ryan_oncall: thanks team. final check: any ongoing 5xx spikes?
emily_csm: one remaining small burst from a 3rd party crawler hitting endpoints, I've asked them to backoff.
jitendra_runtime: we'll add a client-side guidance note to avoid short-interval retries that spike small-batch traffic.
maria_prodeng: follow-up tasks created: T1234 (revert PR and add tests), T1235 (deploy smoke eval), T1236 (autoscaler policy update), T1237 (customer comms).
ryan_oncall: handing off to @maria_prodeng. I am available on pager if needed.
maria_prodeng: taking over. logging final note and scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
